summary: Independent verification of the WorkCard follow-up batch (I1 loop-lock, I2 codebase health test, I3 countdown urgency pulse) + partial Phase E chip standardization. Critical first check: app renders correctly at preview URL — NO stuck black 'LOADING…' splash observed on login page, post-login chat, or /admin panel. The main agent's screenshot-tool hang appears to have been a client/env quirk, not a real bug. I2 pytest (test_codebase_health_score.py) = 12/12 PASS. Loop-safety pytest (-k loop_safety/loop_lock/sweep_expired) = 21 passed / 1 skipped, including test_loop_engine_releases_lock_on_completion_and_failure. I3: CSS `.aurem-countdown-urgent` and `@keyframes aurem-countdown-pulse` (2s cycle, prefers-reduced-motion honored) confirmed defined AND live in the browser (computed `animation-name=aurem-countdown-pulse, animation-duration=2s`). All 3 gate cards (PlanApprovalCard, ShipPendingCard, LoopActionCards user/ship variants) correctly attach the class only when secondsLeft<=60 alongside the existing color shift; card layout unaffected when class absent. Phase E: `.chip`+`.chip-sm`+`.chip-error` renders correctly in browser (color=rgb(252,165,165)=#fca5a5, bg=rgba(239,68,68,0.15), height=20px, font-size=10px, matches spec). ShipLintBadge legacy fallback path also uses #fca5a5 for `blocked` (line 59) — contrast fix reaches non-allowlisted users too, as intended. NOTE: test@aurem.dev maps to user_id=test_admin_001 (the SOLE allowlisted user), so /auth/me returns `workcard_chip_v2_enabled=true` for this account — the flag-OFF fallback path can't be exercised via this preview credential; verified statically that flag-off branch preserves original inline span in both ShipLintBadge (line 79-97) and WorkCard (line 80-93). --border-strong / --ds2-border contrast bumps applied — visually verified across landing page, chat page (with WorkCards, GitHub-revoked banner, project-cleanup banner), admin panel (env/deploy/gh chips, BI cards, sidebar) — no broken borders or regressions.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/main.py is >3200 lines — flagged in prior reports, still a long-term smell (not this batch's job).

The workcard_chip_v2 allowlist has only 1 user (test_admin_001) — since the current dev/preview credential IS that user, most preview testing exercises the flag-ON path. Consider adding a second QA account NOT on the allowlist for future coverage of the fallback branch.
